summary:
TERRA-TRACE (Earth System Trend Detective) is a high-performance, web-based climate telemetry platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge using HTML5, CSS3, and Visual Studio Code, with technical assistance from Gemini.

What We Developed:
A lightweight, zero-CDN-dependency dashboard featuring an interactive orbital map, multi-metric comparison tools (Surface Temperature, Annual Precipitation, and Snow/Glacier Cover), automated statistical significance calculation (p-values), and a dual-language interface (English/Russian).

How It Addresses the Challenge:
It bridges the gap between raw NASA POWER API satellite data and intuitive public access, offering instant visualization of critical environmental changes without the risk of external library failures during demonstrations.

Why It Is Important:
Climate change demands transparent, localized action. By focusing on vulnerable regional ecosystems like the Tien Shan glaciers and the Aral Sea basin, TERRA-TRACE empowers researchers, students, and policymakers to track long-term climate trends accurately, visualize ecological shifts, and make data-driven decisions for our planet's future.
details:
• What it does or how does it work? TERRA-TRACE (Earth System Trend Detective) is an interactive web-based analytics dashboard that monitors and evaluates long-term climate shifts across the globe. It allows users to select preset environmental zones (such as Tian Shan glaciers vs. the Aral Sea basin) or input custom geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) to analyze multi-decadal telemetry data. The application computes linear regression slopes, net changes, and statistical p-values to evaluate trends in surface temperature and precipitation from 1990 onwards.
  • What benefits does it have? It bridges the gap between raw, complex satellite telemetry and actionable environmental insights. By automating statistical significance testing ($p < 0.05$), it helps researchers, students, and enthusiasts immediately distinguish between normal natural variability and statistically proven climate shifts without needing heavy desktop software.
  • What is the intended impact of the project? The project aims to foster climate awareness, empower regional ecological research, and provide an accessible educational tool for students and communities in vulnerable regions (such as Central Asia) to understand environmental transformations firsthand using reliable data models.
    • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
    • Libraries & Frameworks: Chart.js for dynamic neon-styled data visualization and trend plotting.
    • Infrastructure & Hosting: GitHub Pages for public deployment.
    • Data & Architecture: Simulated NASA POWER API telemetry models and local mathematical algorithms for linear regression and p-value calculations, designed to bypass browser/server CORS restrictions seamlessly.
  • How is your project creative? TERRA-TRACE gamifies and simplifies scientific data analysis by framing the user as an "Earth System Trend Detective." Instead of static charts, it features dual-region comparative analysis side-by-side, dynamic time-window filtering (decades), real-time animated counters, and an automated statistical verdict badge that tells the user whether a climate trend is scientifically significant or just noise.
    • Accessibility & Usability: Fully responsive dark-mode UI with dual-language support (English and Russian) to ensure usability across diverse regions.
    • Technical Reliability: Decoupling external telemetry logic to guarantee zero CORS errors and lightning-fast performance across all hosting environments, including mobile and desktop browsers.
    • Scientific Rigor: Implementing standard statistical frameworks (p-value calculation derived from correlation coefficients and degrees of freedom) to ensure mathematical credibility.
